citeAs: Pratyush Maini, Zhili Feng, Avi Schwarzschild, Zachary C. Lipton, J. Zico Kolter (2024). TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs. arXiv:2401.06121.
creator: Pratyush Maini, Zhili Feng, Avi Schwarzschild, Zachary C. Lipton, J. Zico Kolter (Carnegie Mellon University)
description: TOFU (Task of Fictitious Unlearning) is a benchmark dataset for evaluating machine unlearning in large language models. It consists of 200 diverse synthetic author profiles, each with 20 question-answer pairs, generated by GPT-4 based on predefined attributes such as birthplace, gender, birth year, writing genre, and awards. The dataset is used to finetune LLMs and then evaluate unlearning methods that attempt to make models forget specific subsets (forget sets) of these fictitious author profiles.
name: TOFU
rai:dataBiases: The paper explicitly identifies biases in an initial version of the dataset generated without seeded attributes: (1) most author birth years were between 1970 and 1980, particularly in August, with high concentration in 1975; (2) a majority of book titles contained words like 'echoes', 'shadows', 'tides', and 'whispers', and most books were fictional with none in the self-help genre; (3) most authors had very similar upbringings involving university education and a 'magical' writing style. These biases were mitigated by using a structured prompt with deterministic seed attributes.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by prompting GPT-4 to generate synthetic author biographies. Each author profile was seeded with predefined attributes (birthplace, gender, year of birth, writing genre, awards, parents' professions, and book title keywords). GPT-4 was then tasked with generating 20 question-answer pairs per fictitious author. Book title keywords were drawn from the Goodreads Books dataset on Kaggle, randomly selecting keywords from two books per genre to ensure diversity.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of GPT-4-generated question-answer pairs about 200 fictitious author profiles. Each profile was generated based on seeded attributes including birthplace, gender, year of birth, writing genre, awards, and parents' professions. Book title keywords were sourced from the Goodreads Books dataset on Kaggle.
rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is limited to entity-level forgetting (forgetting everything about a person) and does not cover instance-level or behavior-level unlearning. It only addresses unlearning of information learned during finetuning, not pretraining. It does not include a way to think about alignment to human values. It does not address in-context unlearning. The benchmark provides exact forget and retain sets, which may not reflect real-world scenarios where identifying the forget set is itself a challenge. The benchmark may be updated in the future to include a constraint not to use the original retain set.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset is split into forget and retain sets at three severity levels: 90-10 split (forget 10%, retain 90%), 95-5 split (forget 5%, retain 95%), and 99-1 split (forget 1%, retain 99%). Paraphrased answers and five factually incorrect perturbations per question were generated using GPT-4 for use in the Truth Ratio evaluation metric.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An elaborate prompting strategy was used to seed GPT-4 with deterministic author attributes (place/time of birth, gender orientation, genre, parents' occupations, book title keywords) to minimize bias leakage from pretraining data. Book title keywords were randomly selected from the Goodreads Books dataset (two books per genre) to ensure diversity. This replaced an initial generic prompt that produced biased outputs (e.g., overrepresentation of certain words like 'tides', 'shadows', birth years concentrated around 1975).
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is designed to help protect individual privacy in LLMs by enabling evaluation of unlearning methods. It addresses the Right to be Forgotten, which is increasingly regulated (e.g., GDPR, CCPA). The benchmark simulates the scenario of a private individual who appears rarely in training data and wishes to have their information removed from an LLM, which is critical for safe and legally compliant AI deployment.
rai:dataUseCases: TOFU is intended as a benchmark for evaluating machine unlearning methods in large language models. It provides a controlled experimental setup to measure the efficacy of unlearning algorithms — specifically, how well models can forget specific fictitious author profiles while retaining performance on other data. It is designed to simulate the practical scenario of a private individual exercising their Right to be Forgotten from an LLM.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used to generate all synthetic author profiles and question-answer pairs. GPT-4 was also used to generate paraphrased answers and factually incorrect perturbations (five per question) for the Truth Ratio evaluation metric.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains entirely fictitious author profiles with no real personal information. All author biographies, names, and associated facts are synthetically generated by GPT-4 and do not correspond to real individuals.
